paragraphs: Yose ben Shaul and his brothers, Yochanan and Chalafta, were Rav Yosef bar Adda’s students. I did not find Yosef bar Adda anywhere in the Talmud; he himself does not include him among the names Yosef. Some error came before him. He said in Rabbi’s name: Eruvin 81a. ‘When Ravin came, Rabbi Yaakov said: Rabbi Assi said’—it should read Yose ben Shaul; the new Talmud edition did not correct it—‘Rabbi said’: Shabbat 50a, beginning. Rabbi Chiyya bar Gamda said: Rabbi Yose ben Shaul said: Rabbi said; see his entry. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Rabbi Yose ben Shaul said: Rabbi said, in the holy congregation’s name: Beitzah 14b and 27a, Yoma 69, Tamid 27b, where the words ‘Rabbi said’ are absent. He asked Rabbi: Niddah 26b and Avodah Zarah 52b. Rabbi told him: ‘Blessed are you to Heaven, for you have restored my lost article.’ ‘Rav said’: Beitzah 7a. This caused Sheerit Yosef’s author to include him among Rav’s students: he relied on this Gemara and did not notice its error. It seems to me it should read ‘Rabbi said.’ So too appears there on page b: ‘Rabbi Yose ben Shaul also said: Rabbi said,’ and so forth, which does not belong there except that page a had Rabbi Yose ben Shaul saying in Rabbi’s name; therefore it adds ‘Rabbi Yose ben Shaul also said: Rabbi said.’ In Kol HaKelim 125b: Rabbi Yose ben Shaul said, and so forth; Rabbi Yochanan ben Shaul said.
